corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science studies, researchers explore how large language models shape user experience, research methods, education, health communication, and policy. Four recurring strands emerge: human-ai interaction, LLMs as research tools, AI-enabled learning and literacy, and health and governance implications. The literature highlights trust and anthropomorphism concerns, methodological validity issues, benefits for pedagogy, and calls for equity and safety in deployment.

themes.name: Human-AI interaction: trust, embodiment, and governance
themes.description: Explores how human-like versus technical AI features, disclosure, and embodied interfaces influence trust, perceived humanness, dependence, and adoption.

themes.name: LLMs as methodological tools for social science
themes.description: Reviews use of LLMs for coding, sentiment analysis, ethics review, and policy analysis, while addressing validity, calibration, bias, and governance considerations.

themes.name: AI in education and AI literacy
themes.description: Covers AI tutoring, scaffolding, classroom integration, teacher attitudes, student engagement, and the emergence of AI-literacy and assessment challenges.

themes.name: AI in health and public well-being
themes.description: Examines AI-driven health information, misinformation mitigation, patient education tools, and AI-assisted clinical decision support with safety and equity concerns.
